summary: Implements ADR-0148 and ADR-0149 (proposed). Agent 0.37.0 adds the heartbeat block ollama_runners {count, private_mib}: Supervisor.ollamaRunners sums, over every running child whose program is Ollama, the processes of its job object except the child's own pid and the system console host (GetSystemDirectory + conhost.exe, compared by full path), with their private working sets (procMemory). Agent side (B8): only read queries with PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION (QueryFullProcessImageName, K32GetProcessMemoryInfo) on pids taken from the agent's own job; the job is created without a breakaway flag (platform_windows.go newKillOnCloseJob), so a runner cannot leave it to hide; the only excluded program is the system's console host at the system path, which an unprivileged Ollama cannot replace. procTree.members now says whether the job was listed in full; a failed or partial query gives no fact (pids() keeps its old behaviour for existing callers). Unreadable processes still count, so the fact errs towards 'still held'. Router side, agent data (B3, TM-07): poll.note_ollama_runners accepts only a dict with integer count 0..256 and integer private_mib 0..4 TiB (bool excluded), stores a new dict of these two integers (no agent string reaches /admin/state, metrics or the UI), and drops anything else as implausible (ADR-0137 pattern, logged at most every ten minutes); it never raises. Node.runners_known hides a stale value. The fact does not influence routing; it is used for display, two metrics and the unload answer. A compromised agent can therefore make only its own node's unload answer 'released' early (added to TM-07 in threat model EN/DE and the risk register). New route POST /admin/nodes/{fp}/unload (B2, TM-03): registered before the generic node action and protected like every admin write by basic_auth_middleware (every non-/v1/ path: admin_networks, Basic Auth) and the X-Skirnir-UI header check for non-GET /admin/*; tests show 401 without credentials and 403 without the header, and neither reaches Ollama. Preconditions are checked before any effect (unknown fp 404, not approved 409, offline, OpenAI upstream, no fresh runner fact, unload already running, measurement or benchmark on the node 409; malformed or non-object body 400). The action sends keep_alive 0 for the model names from that node's own /api/ps back to the same node through perf._ollama (the existing measurement path, an allowed tunnel path), then answers released only with a heartbeat received after /api/ps emptied. Resource bound (TM-08): one unload per node at a time (RUNNING set, cleared in finally also on cancellation), timeout_s at most 600, polling every 0.5 s; admin-only. Logs and journal carry node name, fixed reason values and model names. Findings fixed before publication: (1) a malformed JSON body was read as None and defaulted to an empty body, so a garbled request would still unload; now 400, tested. (2) Parallel unloads of the same node could multiply the /api/ps polling through its tunnel for up to 600 s each; now one at a time per node with 409, tested including cancellation. Pre-existing and unchanged: model names from a node's /api/ps reach the log unescaped, as in poll.busy_unload_check and perf.

tests.command: python test/selftest_ollama_runners.py (new, in ci.yml python job)
tests.evidence: all checks pass: heartbeat block stored, 13 rejected value shapes dropped as implausible while GPU values still apply, stale heartbeat hides the fact, node view and both metrics (absent for a node without the fact); timeout_s validation (9 rejected values); every 409 refusal before Ollama is asked; release only with a heartbeat after the empty /api/ps (mutation removing the hb_ts check fails the test); timeout, timeout with loaded, not_reported, offline, 502; HTTP 404/409/400 incl. malformed JSON, 200, 503, journal entry; second concurrent unload 409 and guard cleared after the answer and after cancellation; route resolves to unload.handle_unload; 401 without credentials and 403 without X-Skirnir-UI, neither reaching Ollama.

tests.evidence: no Go toolchain in the local WSL distribution and no container run here; CI's go (Linux and Windows) and container jobs run them.

limitations: No real Ollama was used (the task forbids testing against personal infrastructure): the runner classification is tested with the test binary as server and runner in real job objects, not with ollama.exe and its runners; a future Ollama helper process in the job would keep the count above 0 (safe direction, unload then times out).
The agent's fact cannot be verified by the router; a compromised agent can claim its own node's memory released early (TM-07).
The count is node-wide; per-model attribution is out of scope (ADR-0148).
Linux agents report no block, so the unload is refused there with 409.
